question: In figure, bisectors of \(\angle P\) and \(\angle Q\) intersect at point \(O\) and \(\angle R = 40^\circ\), then \(\angle POQ = \text{what}\)?
options: [{"label":"a","text":"[There is an image]","is_correct":true},{"label":"b","text":"[There is an image]","is_correct":false},{"label":"c","text":"[There is an image]","is_correct":false},{"label":"d","text":"[There is an image]","is_correct":false}]
explanation: In \(\triangle PQR\), the sum of angles is 180°. So, \(\angle P + \angle Q = 180^\circ - 40^\circ = 140^\circ\). Their bisectors give \(\frac{1}{2} \angle P + \frac{1}{2} \angle Q = 70^\circ\). In \(\triangle POQ\), \(\frac{1}{2} \angle P + \frac{1}{2} \angle Q + \angle POQ = 180^\circ\), so \(70^\circ + \angle POQ = 180^\circ\), hence \(\angle POQ = 110^\circ\).

question: Two bisectors of the angles \(\angle Q\) and \(\angle R\) of triangle \(\triangle PQR\) intersect at point \(O\) if \(\angle P = 50^\circ\), then \(\angle QOR = ?\)

explanation: In \(\triangle PQR\), \(\angle Q + \angle R = 180^\circ - 50^\circ = 130^\circ\). Their bisectors give \(\frac{1}{2} \angle Q + \frac{1}{2} \angle R = 65^\circ\).
